cards.text: The prophet Isaiah is passing along the LORD's own words, and they open like somebody shouting down a busy street. The LORD calls out, "Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters". And He's not done calling people in.

cards.question: The LORD also calls out to people who have no money at all. What does He tell them to do?
True or false: the wine and milk the LORD offers will cost them something.

cards.text: Wine and milk, "without money and without cost". Friend, the expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with would've FAINTED right on the spot.
Then the LORD turns to what people have been spending their money and their hard work on.

cards.question: The LORD asks why people spend their money and their work on certain things. What's the trouble with those things?

cards.text: Money and hard work on stuff that doesn't satisfy. I spent YEARS in that drawer surrounded by takeout menus from places that closed, and not ONE of them ever filled me up.

cards.question: Instead of chasing what doesn't satisfy, what does the LORD tell them to do?

cards.text: Listen and eat what is good, He says, and your soul will delight in the richest of foods. Then He says it again: lean in, come to Him, and listen, so your soul may live.

cards.question: The LORD promises to make a covenant with them. He says that covenant will last ___.

cards.text: An everlasting covenant, with the loving devotion He promised to David, Israel's king. Not a trial offer, friend. EVERLASTING.

cards.question: The LORD says He has made David a ___ to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples.
Now the LORD speaks to the people listening. What will nations who do not know them do?
True or false: those nations come because the LORD has bestowed glory on the people.

cards.text: Nations RUNNING to them. Friend, nobody ever ran to my junk drawer except to grab the tape and slam it shut.
Now the message turns into a call to act while the door is open. "Seek the LORD while He may be found; call on Him while He is near."

cards.question: Next comes a call to forsake his way and his thoughts and return to the LORD. Who is it aimed at?
When he returns to the LORD, our God will have compassion and will ___ pardon him.

cards.text: FREELY pardon, friend. No hold music, and no "we'll get back to you in six to eight weeks."

cards.question: Then the LORD speaks up about Himself. True or false: He says His thoughts are the same as our thoughts.
The LORD says His ways and thoughts are higher than ours. What does He compare that to?

cards.text: THAT high. On a good day, MY thoughts reach the top of the cookie jar, and only if I hop.
Now the LORD paints a picture from the weather: rain and snow falling from heaven.

cards.question: True or false: the rain and snow go back up without ever watering the earth.

cards.text: They water the earth so it buds and sprouts and gives seed to sow and food to eat. And the LORD says something that comes from His own mouth works just the same.

cards.question: Just like the rain, the LORD says His ___ will not return to Him empty.
The LORD's word will accomplish what He pleases. What does He say it will do where He sends it?
The message closes with the people heading out. They will go out with ___ and be led forth in ___.

cards.text: The mountains and hills will burst into song before them, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands. Friend, I can't get ONE round of applause out of a cookie sheet.
Then the land itself changes. Instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow, and instead of the brier, the myrtle will spring up.

cards.question: The LORD says all this will make a name for Him. What kind of sign will it be?

answers.text: A sign that fades in time

cards.text: Everlasting, never to be destroyed. After years under the dust in a junk drawer, friend, nothing sounds sweeter than that.

findings.problem: Recap card. It repeats 'without money and without cost' from verse 1, which card 3 just asked about, and adds a joke. It doesn't move the baker forward to anything new in the passage.
Recap card. It restates card 6's answer ('Money and hard work on stuff that doesn't satisfy') and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from verse 2.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the fact. Verse 2 is about spending money and labor on what doesn't satisfy. The comparison is about lying near takeout menus that never 'filled me up', and nobody spent anything. The line also brings in eating non-cookie food through the menus.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'Now the LORD speaks to the people listening' decides who the 'you' in verse 5 is. The text leaves it open: it follows straight on from the lines about David, and BSB just says 'you'. Card 14 repeats this with 'bestowed glory on the people'.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Recap card. 'Nations RUNNING to them' restates card 13's answer and adds a joke. Nothing new from verse 5 is told.
The text says 'that He may have compassion'. The question turns this into a firm 'our God will have compassion'.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Recap card. 'FREELY pardon' repeats card 3's answer and adds a joke. Nothing new from the passage is told.

The joke's action doesn't match the fact. 'Freely pardon' is about pardon given generously. The comparison (hold music, 'six to eight weeks') is about waiting and speed, which suggests the text says the pardon comes fast.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Recap card. 'THAT high' plus a joke repeats card 6's answer and tells nothing new from verse 9.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The setup for card 11 says the thing 'comes from His own mouth'. That rules out the wrong answer 'glory', which doesn't come from a mouth. Only 'word' and 'breath' are left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Mostly a recap. 'Everlasting' repeats card 16's answer, and the rest is a reaction. Only 'never to be destroyed' is new. That phrase could be told on card 16's setup or on card 17 as its own beat, without repeating the answer.
